claim: In the Munschauer et al. study, NORAD was reported to localize equally between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

claim: HCT116 cell line was used in both the Lee et al., 2016 and Munschauer et al., 2018 studies.

claim: A cell-type specific difference in NORAD trafficking is not the cause of the discordant localization results between studies.
source: arguing against a cell-type specific difference in NORAD trafficking as the cause of these discordant results.

claim: The disparate observed localization patterns could be due to unrecognized processing of the NORAD transcript.
source: We considered the possibility that the disparate observed localization patterns could be due to unrecognized processing of the NORAD transcript, such that different segments of the RNA that are recognized by the different FISH probes accumulate in distinct subcellular compartments.

claim: A panel of 11 in vitro transcribed RNA FISH probes spanning the complete NORAD sequence was generated.
source: we generated a panel of 11 in vitro transcribed RNA FISH probes spanning the complete NORAD sequence (Figure 1A) (Mito et al., 2016).

claim: One NORAD FISH probe (probe 7) that recognized a segment containing an Alu repeat element gave rise to a nonspecific nuclear signal present in both NORAD+/+ and NORAD–/– HCT116 cells.
source: One probe, that recognized a segment of NORAD containing an Alu repeat element (probe 7), gave rise to a nonspecific nuclear signal that was present in both NORAD+/+ and NORAD–/– HCT116 cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The remaining 10 NORAD FISH probes produced a highly consistent, predominantly cytoplasmic, punctate localization pattern in wild-type cells that was absent in NORAD–/– cells.
source: The remaining 10 probes produced a highly consistent, predominantly cytoplasmic, punctate localization pattern in wild-type cells that was absent in NORAD–/– cells (Figure 1A–B).

claim: Subcellular fractionation followed by qRT-PCR using primers located at the 3′ or 5′ ends of NORAD revealed that 80–90% of the transcript is localized to the cytoplasmic compartment.
source: These results were confirmed using subcellular fractionation followed by quantitative reverse transcriptase-PCR (qRT-PCR) using primers located at the 3′ or 5′ ends of NORAD, which revealed that 80–90% of the transcript is localized to the cytoplasmic compartment (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: RNA FISH using the panel of probes spanning NORAD revealed clear cytoplasmic localization after treatment with doxorubicin or camptothecin, without a significant increase in nuclear signal compared to untreated cells.
source: RNA FISH using the panel of probes spanning NORAD revealed clear cytoplasmic localization after treatment with doxorubicin or camptothecin, without a significant increase in nuclear signal compared to untreated cells (Figure 2A–B).

claim: A clear increase in cytoplasmic NORAD signal was apparent in cells treated with DNA damaging agents.
source: Consistent with the previously reported induction of NORAD after DNA damage (Lee et al., 2016), a clear increase in cytoplasmic NORAD signal was apparent in treated cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and is consistent with previous findings.

claim: Subcellular fractionation experiments following treatment with DNA damaging agents confirmed that NORAD remained predominantly in the cytoplasmic compartment at all time points.
source: These findings were further corroborated by subcellular fractionation experiments following treatment with DNA damaging agents, which confirmed that NORAD remained predominantly in the cytoplasmic compartment at all time points (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).

claim: A modest increase in nuclear NORAD levels was observed that peaked after 12 hr of camptothecin or doxorubicin treatment.
source: Interestingly, we observed a modest increase in nuclear NORAD levels that peaked after 12 hr of camptothecin or doxorubicin treatment.

claim: The modest increase in nuclear NORAD might represent a burst of NORAD transcription in response to accumulating DNA damage.
source: We speculated that this might represent a burst of NORAD transcription in response to accumulating DNA damage.
evidence: This is stated as speculation by the authors.

claim: Co-treatment of cells with DNA damaging agents and actinomycin D completely abrogated any detectable increase in nuclear NORAD abundance in treated cells.

claim: NORAD is a predominantly cytoplasmic RNA in HCT116 cells and does not detectably redistribute to the nucleus upon DNA damage.

claim: The localization findings are consistent with the reported localization of NORAD in other human and mouse cell lines.
source: These findings are consistent with the reported localization of NORAD in other human and mouse cell lines (Kopp et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2016; Tichon et al., 2016).

claim: The disparate localization pattern observed using a commercially-available RNA FISH probe set most likely represented a non-specific signal.

source: Since these RAP-MS experiments utilized pulse labeling with 4-thiouridine to crosslink NORAD to protein interactors

source: a bias towards detection of proteins that bind to newly synthesized NORAD would be expected, potentially explaining the enrichment of nuclear interactors observed.

Peptides were identified and scored using a combined algorithm that employed three search engines (Sequest HT, Mascot, and MS Amanda). Isoforms of PUM1 and PUM2, along with RBMX, were indeed identified as significantly-enriched interacting partners of NORAD compared to RMRP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: The increase in NORAD levels upon RBMX depletion may be an indirect effect of the previously reported accumulation of DNA damage caused by RBMX loss of function.
source: We speculate that this increase in NORAD levels may be an indirect effect of the previously reported accumulation of DNA damage caused by RBMX loss of function (Adamson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as speculation by the authors with citation to Adamson et al., 2012.

claim: RBMX knockdown did not alter the predominantly cytoplasmic localization of NORAD.
source: Additionally, RBMX knockdown did not alter the predominantly cytoplasmic localization of NORAD, as indicated by subcellular fractionation experiments (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: RBMX is not an essential co-factor for NORAD expression or localization.
source: We conclude that RBMX is not an essential co-factor for NORAD expression or localization.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: These results establish the essential role of PUM binding for the regulation of genomic stability by NORAD.
source: In sum, these results establish the essential role of PUM binding for the regulation of genomic stability by NORAD.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: A systematic examination of the subcellular localization of NORAD unequivocally established its predominantly cytoplasmic localization under baseline conditions as well as after treatment with DNA-damaging agents.
source: A systematic examination of the subcellular localization of this lncRNA unequivocally established its predominantly cytoplasmic localization under baseline conditions as well as after treatment with DNA-damaging agents.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Genetic complementation experiments demonstrated that PUM binding is essential, whereas RBMX interaction is dispensable, for the genome maintenance function of NORAD.
source: Moreover, genetic complementation experiments demonstrated that PUM binding is essential, whereas RBMX interaction is dispensable, for the genome maintenance function of NORAD.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented.

claim: These results further define and clarify the NORAD molecular mechanism of action.
source: These results further define and clarify the NORAD molecular mechanism of action
evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: These results direct future investigation towards elucidation of the regulation and physiologic roles of the NORAD:PUM axis.
source: and direct future investigation towards elucidation of the regulation and physiologic roles of the NORAD:PUM axis.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions based on the findings.
